content: At a suit contract, count losers hand-by-hand in the long trump hand. For each loser ask: can I ruff it, discard it on a side winner, or finesse to avoid it? Turn losers into winners before you touch trumps if dummy's ruffs are the answer.

metadata.sourceDocument: Watson — Planning the Play, At a Suit Contract

content: At notrump, count sure winners first. If they fall short of the contract, pick the suit that can develop the extra tricks with the fewest losses and the entries to enjoy it — then attack it early, before the opponents set up theirs.

metadata.sourceDocument: Watson — Planning the Play, At a No-trump Contract

content: Count the hand: track each suit's distribution as cards appear, and use the bidding to place missing honors. Knowing exactly how the enemy cards lie lets you finesse the right way, drop a doubleton King, or execute an end play.

Do not finesse out of habit. If you can count enough tricks without risk, take the safe line. Sometimes playing for a defender's honor to drop, or cashing sure winners, beats a fifty-fifty finesse — especially when a loser is affordable.

The contract is the thing. Play to make your contract first; overtricks come second. Choose the line that most safely brings home the tricks you actually need, even if a greedier line might win one more.

metadata.sourceDocument: Watson — General Principles: The Contract Is the Thing

content: Pause before trick one. What is your contract, and what is your plan to bring it home?
